subtitle: Give agents hands: the Model Context Protocol, tool schemas, permissions, and safe execution patterns for catalog and order operations
audience: Developers who finished LangGraph for E-commerce (tools chapter) and Prompt Engineering 101, now standardizing agent integrations. Version basis stated once, used everywhere: MCP spec 2026-07-28 + TypeScript SDK v2 (@modelcontextprotocol/server, zod v4, Node 20+). Protocol machinery runs as executable JS in the playground; SDK code targets your Node project.
outcomes: Explain why MCP exists (N×M integrations) and how it differs from bespoke function calling
Map the architecture: host, clients, servers, transports (stdio vs Streamable HTTP), JSON-RPC + discovery
Define tools with registerTool: names, descriptions, Zod input schemas, titles, and annotations
Expose catalog data as resources (URIs, direct vs tool-mediated) and prompts as reusable templates
Scope permissions per tool, gate destructive operations, and use elicitation for confirmations
Execute safely: SDK validation, timeouts, idempotency keys, audit logging, isError discipline
Build a store MCP server (catalog lookup + order tools) with the v2 SDK
Debug with the Inspector, tracing, version negotiation, and error-code reading
Evaluate tool-calling end to end: selection accuracy, argument validity, and safe-failure paths
Ship an order-operations MCP server consumed by an agent, measured and audited

assessment.q: Twelve hosts × eight data sources, all bespoke integrations. MCP changes the math how?
options: Standard client↔server protocol: N hosts + M servers integrate N+M ways instead of N×M bespoke wirings
assessment.explain: Standards collapse integration matrices: each side implements the protocol once. N+M vs N×M is MCP's entire economic argument (Ch.1).

assessment.q: Host vs client vs server in MCP?
options: Host runs the AI app and owns one client per server; clients hold connections; servers expose tools/resources/prompts
assessment.explain: VS Code (host) spawns a client per server (filesystem, Sentry); servers serve context. One client per connection (Ch.2).

assessment.q: stdio vs Streamable HTTP transport — choose per case.
options: Local single-client process integration → stdio; remote multi-client with HTTP auth → Streamable HTTP
assessment.explain: Locality + client count + auth needs decide: stdio (same machine, one client, no network) vs HTTP (remote, many clients, bearer/OAuth) (Ch.2).

options: v2 registerTool(name, config, handler) replaces v1 tool(); one Zod inputSchema yields advertised JSON Schema + pre-handler validation + inferred arg types
assessment.explain: Migration fact with teeth: single-schema source of truth (advertise + validate + infer). v1 code needs the codemod (Ch.3).

assessment.q: lookup_order vs search_orders undescribed. Predict + fix?
options: Model mis-selects between overlapping tools — describe selection criteria per tool (when-each); descriptions are the only docs the model gets
assessment.explain: .describe() survives into advertised JSON Schema: argument docs reach the model. Sibling disambiguation lives in descriptions (Ch.3).

assessment.q: Catalog text for grounding: resource vs tool?
options: Stable reference data → resources (direct reads, URIs); computed/filtered/live lookups → tools (Ch.4).
assessment.explain: Direct context (files, rows, policy text) reads as resources; actions/computations invoke as tools. Shape follows access pattern.

assessment.q: issue_refund in an agent's hands, no gate. Design?
options: Gated destructive tool: permission scope + approval (elicitation/HITL) + audit log + idempotency — money moves under supervision
assessment.explain: Destructive tools need scopes, gates, and audit trails. Least privilege + approval paths (Ch.6).

assessment.q: Tool throws on invalid stock ID. Correct result shape?
options: {content: [...explaining...], isError: true} — failures as readable results the model can react to, never raw crashes
assessment.explain: isError results keep failures inside the protocol: readable, routable, loggable. Crashes break runs opaquely (Ch.7).

assessment.q: Same ticket re-runs issue_refund after a crash. Prevention?
options: Idempotency keys + check-before-act: re-execution returns the recorded outcome instead of double-charging
assessment.explain: Retries/replays re-invoke tools: keys make repeats safe. Money tools without idempotency double-apply on recovery (Ch.7).

assessment.q: Sampling in new server code (2026-07-28 spec). Verdict?
options: Deprecated — integrate LLM provider APIs directly instead of sampling/createMessage
assessment.explain: Spec-deprecated client primitive: new code calls providers directly. Elicitation remains for user input (Ch.2/6).

assessment.q: Tool list changed mid-conversation (new refund policy tool). How does the client learn?
options: Opt-in subscriptions/listen for toolsListChanged → re-list on notification (plus polling fallback; best-effort delivery)
assessment.explain: Dynamic capabilities via opt-in notification streams with re-list on event; best-effort means polling backs it up (Ch.9).

assessment.q: stdout vs stderr in a stdio MCP server?
options: stdout carries the protocol (JSON-RPC) — polluting it corrupts messages; log to stderr (or OpenTelemetry)
assessment.explain: Transport hygiene: stdout is the wire. Logging there breaks framing; stderr/OpenTelemetry keeps observability without corruption (Ch.7/9).

project.title: The Order-Operations MCP Server
project.summary: Ship a version-pinned MCP server (spec 2026-07-28, TS SDK v2) exposing catalog lookup, order tools (read + gated refund), a policy resource, and a triage prompt — consumed by an agent loop with routing tests, approval gates, audit logging, and an evaluation report. Standards-compliant hands for e-commerce agents.
requirements: Server: McpServer (name/version) with 4+ tools (catalog search, order lookup, gated refund, shipment tracking), 1+ resource (policy text), 1+ prompt (triage template)
Schemas: Zod input schemas with .describe() on every argument; outputSchema + structuredContent on lookups; closed shapes
Permissions: refund tool gated (approval via elicitation/HITL design); tool audit (least-privilege manifest per consumer)
Safety: SDK validation first, timeouts, idempotency keys on money tools, isError discipline, stderr-only logging
Consumer: agent loop (route → call → validate → generate) with routing tests and loop budgets
Evaluation: tool-selection accuracy, argument-validity rate, safe-failure paths (invalid/unknown/refused), per-segment report
technical: Package basis: @modelcontextprotocol/server (v2), zod/v4, Node 20+, type: module; stdio transport (Streamable HTTP noted as extension)
Protocol machinery (validators, gates, audit) also demonstrated as runnable JS
Threads/conversations isolated; audit log append-only with tool/args/outcome per call
Numbers reproducible: gold tool-call set + router tests committed
project.architecture: Four sections: (1) Server map — tools/resources/prompts with schemas and permission rationale; (2) Consumer loop — routing, calls, validation, gates with traces; (3) Evaluation — selection accuracy, arg validity, safe-failure paths per segment; (4) Operations — version pinning, Inspector workflow, audit-log design, upgrade notes (v1→v2).
steps: scaffold with createServer factory + one read-only tool; verify with Inspector
Add catalog/order tools with Zod schemas and descriptions; test invalid args (SDK rejects pre-handler)
Add policy resource + triage prompt; wire the consumer loop with routing tests
Gate the refund tool (approval + idempotency + audit); demonstrate approve/edit/skip
Build the gold tool-call set; baseline selection/validity/safety; iterate once; re-score
Write operations (pinning, Inspector, audit) and the findings memo
evaluation: All tools schema-closed with described args; outputSchema on lookups
Refund gated with approval path demonstrated; idempotency proven by re-run
Gold baseline + iteration with per-segment diffs; safe-failure paths all covered
Audit log complete per call (tool/args/outcome); stdout clean (protocol only)
stretch: Add Streamable HTTP transport with bearer auth and document the trade-offs vs stdio
Implement elicitation confirmation for refunds with a scripted user simulator
Add Tasks-extension handling for a long-running inventory reconciliation job

interviewQs.q: Why does MCP exist when we already had function calling?
interviewQs.a: Function calling standardizes model→tool syntax per provider; MCP standardizes the whole integration surface (discovery, tools, resources, prompts, transports, versions) across hosts and servers. One function-calling integration serves one provider's models; one MCP server serves every host (Claude Code, VS Code, Cursor, custom apps). N+M vs N×M — plus resources/prompts, which function calling never covered.

interviewQs.q: registerTool vs tool() — what changed and why does it matter?
interviewQs.a: TS SDK v2's registerTool(name, config, handler) replaces v1's tool(): one Zod inputSchema now yields the advertised JSON Schema, pre-handler argument validation, and inferred handler types. It matters because validation moved into the framework — bad arguments reject before handlers run (fail fast with model-readable errors), and .describe() text becomes the model's only argument documentation. Migration needs the codemod plus package rename (@modelcontextprotocol/server).

interviewQs.q: Design permissions for catalog lookup vs refund issuance.
interviewQs.a: Lookup: read-only, ungated, broadly available (annotation readOnlyHint). Refund: destructive — scoped to finance consumers, approval-gated (elicitation/HITL over thresholds), idempotency-keyed, audit-logged per call. Selection tests prove agents pick correctly; gold attack items prove pressure tickets can't bypass the gate. Least privilege per consumer, validated at boundaries.

interviewQs.q: Sampling is deprecated — what do you do instead, and what remains for user input?
interviewQs.a: Servers needing LLM completions call provider APIs directly (spec 2026-07-28 deprecated sampling/createMessage). User input stays via elicitation (elicitation/create with schemas) — servers requesting confirmation or details through the client. Confusing the two (sampling for confirmations) was always wrong; the deprecation just makes it official.

interviewQs.q: Stdio vs Streamable HTTP for a store's order-tools server?
interviewQs.a: Same-machine single assistant (Claude Desktop + local inventory DB): stdio — no network, one client, simplest ops, stdout-discipline required. Multi-agent backend service with many clients + auth: Streamable HTTP with OAuth/bearer — remote, many clients, standard HTTP security. Decide by locality, client count, and auth needs; the JSON-RPC protocol is identical either way.

interviewQs.q: A tool throws on bad input mid-conversation. Correct handling end to end?
interviewQs.a: Never throw across the protocol: return {content: [...readable...], isError: true} so the model can react (clarify, retry with fixed args, escalate). Validate pre-handler via schemas (most bad input never reaches code), log the failure with args, and cover the path in gold safe-failure items. Crashes break runs opaquely; isError results keep them debuggable and routable.
